releases.title: Clearer Atlas workspace
notes: Home shows model readiness, current work and useful next actions.
Desktop and Android share clearer navigation, readable controls and the Atlas droid.
Mission results distinguish reported progress, evidence, pending approvals and offline state.
Desktop supports compact windows, larger text and clearer model setup states.
Text-only drafts restore without phantom images. Local demo chat reconnects after backgrounding. Android refines memory and desktop linking.

releases.title: Nocturne and Raevin
notes: Nocturne brings obsidian surfaces, silver typography and restrained blue light to desktop and Android.
Android gains refined Chat, Projects, Home and Signals screens, plus updated pairing, memory, libraries, launcher and widget.
Raevin uses a natural charcoal raven with blue wing particles and 32 smoothly blended gestures.
Desktop chat, workspace, Build Studio, memory, model setup and quick commands share the new visual direction.
Reduced motion, phone lifecycle and battery-saving behavior remain supported.
The app keeps its existing pairing, package identity and Hey Atlas wake phrase. Repeated wake detection remains experimental.

releases.title: Verified update packaging and phone repairs
notes: Compressed native libraries keep the Android APK within the existing updater limit, with all four CPU architectures retained.
Builds check APK size, and release preflight validates bounded notes before creating version tags.
Local voice selects the optional fidelity model using its corrected checksum.
Offline English speech setup, alarm scheduling, draft recovery and approval/photo controls include recent repairs.
Shared encrypted memory, the Brain view, desktop chat and companion improvements are included.
Hey Atlas standby remains experimental: repeated wake detection is not reliable on the tested phone.

releases.title: Update packaging and phone reliability
notes: Compressed native libraries keep the Android download within the existing updater size limit, with all supported CPU architectures retained.
Android builds check the APK size before it can reach release staging.
Local voice model selection, offline speech setup, alarm scheduling and approval controls include the recent Android repairs.
Hey Atlas standby remains experimental: repeated wake detection is not reliable on the tested phone.

releases.title: One assistant, durable memory and local voice
notes: Shared encrypted memory gains a Brain map, full-archive search and source-linked decisions and open questions.
Desktop chat supports readable controls, resizing, maximize and bounded speech cards; droid animations use calm idle poses and amber thinking instruments.
Optional Supertonic 3 provides CPU speech in 31 languages. Connected-phone replies use the selected desktop voice; local Android voice remains Kokoro.
Android Live Talk handles offline language errors and offers opt-in Hey Atlas standby with a visible microphone service.
Atlas-owned alarms and configured morning weather/news briefings use local phone audio. Location and sources are user settings.
Website builds wait for a confirmed brief, show elapsed progress, support cancellation and verify saved image references and mobile CSS.
Release provenance binds the complete private source commit to matching signed desktop updates, APKs, versioned installers and public metadata.

releases.title: Shared memory and approved desktop actions
notes: Phone and desktop conversations share an encrypted desktop archive with bounded sync, deletion tombstones and local phone caching.
An idle conversation editor preserves concise context for older chats while leaving the original turns encrypted and intact.
Windows Search result selection, named accessibility controls and local OCR provide approved actions in selected apps.
Paired Android requests can authorize a single web turn or explicitly enable web access until /web off.
The optional Ming Image workflow plans website assets, renders locally while the main brain rests and restores it before site construction.
An Atlas-branded Windows setup verifies prerequisites and creates a first-time Companion install without manual Python setup.

releases.title: Atlas operates across desktop and phone
notes: The amber companion adds a local first-run model chooser, with hardware fit estimates, explicit download consent and integrity checks.
Studio gains selected Windows control guidance, engineering missions with chosen tests, output watches, mid-plan changes, and honest project checkpoints.
Bounded OBS and Blender adapters, expiring phone conversation handoff, and encrypted Pocket Projects extend the approved desktop-to-phone workflow.
Smart Roam uses a private coarse layout scan to avoid busy screen areas. Quiet visuals pauses continuous effects while retaining deliberate roaming.

releases.title: Pocket Tools display fix
notes: Android Pocket Tools now paints its saved tool and keeps its native controls visible on affected phones.
A real paired Studio tool was downloaded, edited and reopened on a OnePlus 15. Its phone-side edit persisted.
The desktop companion behavior is unchanged; this signed desktop archive aligns the source, version and release documentation.

releases.title: A companion across desktop and phone
notes: The companion can move across both displays. Speech subtly favors the display where Atlas is standing.
Studio tools can be shared explicitly to paired Android devices and saved there for offline use.
An authenticated PC starter can launch the companion from Android while Windows is awake and signed in.
Android adds local alarms in Atlas's voice, timers and encrypted notes with phone-side approval.
